name: Tennis elbow (lateral elbow pain)
goal: Settle pain at the outside of the elbow and strengthen the forearm tendon gradually, while easing off the gripping that aggravates it. Recovery usually takes weeks to a few months.
whoFor: People with tennis elbow (lateral elbow tendinopathy): pain at the outside of the elbow when gripping, lifting or typing, without having to play tennis.
notFor: Pain after a fall onto the arm that hasn't been checked
trackedMetric: Elbow pain when gripping or lifting (0-10)
painRules: Up to about 3 out of 10 during exercise is OK if it settles within an hour and isn't worse the next day. Meanwhile, lift with palms up and avoid long, hard gripping.
redFlags: Numbness, tingling or weakness in the hand or fingers
Pain after a fall or injury, or you can't straighten the elbow
A hot, red, swollen elbow, or fever
Neck pain with pain spreading down the arm

phases.name: Settle with holds
phases.exitCriteria: Holds are comfortable and gripping hurts less.

phases.name: Slow strength
phases.exitCriteria: Slow lifts with your target weight at 3 out of 10 or less.

items.note: Shoulder strength helps take load off the elbow.

phases.name: Back to full use
phases.exitCriteria: Gripping, lifting and your sport feel normal. Keep strength work twice a week.

references: Coombes BK, Bisset L, Vicenzino B. 2015. Management of lateral elbow tendinopathy: one size does not fit all. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 45:938-49.
